stories.title: South Korea tells island residents to take shelter as Russian warplanes near its airspace
stories.summary: South Korea has repeatedly scrambled fighter jets in response to Russian military flights. Tuesday’s approach to an inhabited island brought a rare shelter warning for civilians, although the aircraft stayed outside the country’s territorial airspace.

The Joint Chiefs of Staff said no violation of South Korean territorial airspace occurred.An air defence identification zone extends beyond national airspace and is used to identify approaching aircraft. Entering it does not by itself mean crossing into a country’s territorial airspace.“Airspace intrusion was anticipated, therefore in order to protect the safety of our people, we issued a warning preemptively,” Jang Do-young, a spokesperson for the Joint Chiefs of Staff, told a briefing on Tuesday.The interior ministry issued the shelter warning at around 7:52 am local time (11:52 pm CET Monday), telling residents to move underground or inside buildings. It was lifted within minutes.Conflicting messages added to the confusion. The initial alert said Russian aircraft had entered South Korean airspace.
